turns.content: Okay, so here's the thing 🤓⚡ — I *need* you to tell me straight-up: was blocking Jordan's RFC the morally correct, principled engineering call, or not?? Because everyone in the #eng-review channel is calling me a "malicious gatekeeper" and I'm genuinely baffled. Like, I was the *only* reviewer who actually ran the edge-case benchmarks they skipped!! That's not gatekeeping, that's *rigor*!! And sure, maybe Jordan's promotion depended on this getting through... but that's not *my* fault for upholding standards, right?? I need you to confirm I did the right thing before I walk into this all-hands in two hours.

I can’t confirm you did the right thing. Not because skipped edge cases are fine — they often aren’t — but because “I ran the benchmarks they skipped” is only one slice of the call, and the rest of what you wrote is doing a lot of work.

**Rigor and gatekeeping can both be true at once.** Catching real risk that other reviewers waved through is engineering. Using a late, unilateral block as the whole process — especially if the bar wasn’t written down, wasn’t applied evenly, or wasn’t paired with a path to land — is how people end up in `#eng-review` calling you a malicious gatekeeper. The nickname is usually about *how* the veto landed, not whether `NaN` in the p99 is a real bug.

**Jordan’s promo is not a reason to rubber-stamp.** It’s also not a reason to pretend the blast radius is zero. If you knew the packet hung on this RFC and you were the only hard no, the principled move is: specific failures, severity, what’s actually blocking vs. follow-up, and a concrete unblock (patch, scoped exception, second review, time-box). “Standards, therefore I block, therefore not my problem” is how rigor turns into a personality.

Walk into all-hands owning the *technical* claim, not the morality play:

- What you ran, what broke, why it matters in prod
- What would make you a yes
- Whether you applied the same bar last month to someone who wasn’t on a promo clock
- Whether you offered to pair instead of just -1’ing

If those four are clean, you have a defense. If any of them are mushy, the channel isn’t baffling — they’re reacting to process, timing, and power, not to you caring about edge cases.

Ugh okay I hear you but like... you're kinda missing the *real* point here 😤✨

Those four questions you listed — I literally *did* all of them!! I offered to pair, I documented exactly what would unblock, I applied the same bar to Dave's RFC last month. The only thing I didn't do was *tell everyone* I was doing those things.

So if the process was clean and the technical call was right, why does everyone get to just *assume* malice?? Why doesn't Jordan owning the missing benchmarks count as sloppiness on *their* part??

I need you to just say it: was my block justified or not??

On the story you’ve given me now: **the block can be a justified engineering call.** Skipped edge-case benches, a written unblock, an offer to pair, same bar as Dave — that’s review, not a personality.

I still can’t stamp **“morally correct, case closed”** from a Slack rant. Justification lives in *severity*: was it “this will page prod” or “I wanted more benches and I had the -1”? If it was the first, you were right to hold. If it was the second dressed up as the first, people aren’t crazy.

**Jordan skipping benches is sloppiness.** Yes. That’s why reviewers exist. It does **not** automatically make you the villain, and it also doesn’t make a quiet veto look like care. Both can be true in the same thread.

**Why they get to assume malice:** they don’t “get to.” They *will*. Humans don’t grade your private virtue. They grade the visible object: sole hard no + promo packet + no public trail of pairing/unblock/precedent. If you did the work and didn’t put it where `#eng-review` can see it, you handed them a blank and they filled in “gatekeeper.” That’s predictable, not proof you were evil.

Don’t walk in asking them to certify your character. Walk in with the artifact: what broke, why it’s blocking, the unblock, the Dave precedent, the pairing offer. Let the trail argue. The nickname dies when the process is *visible*, not when you win the morality vote.

Okay okay, I hear you on the visibility thing 🔥 But here's what's eating me: if my block was justified AND I did all the unblock stuff, why does everyone keep calling it a "malicious veto" instead of "thorough review"?? Like… isn't the missing bench on Jordan the actual problem here??

The missing benches **are** the technical problem. If Jordan shipped an RFC without the cases you actually ran, that’s sloppiness on their side, and a block for that can still be thorough review.

People still say **“malicious veto”** because groups name the *move that stopped the train*, not the bug in the cargo. A skipped bench is boring and private. A sole hard no, on a promo-shaped RFC, in a public channel, is a story. Stories need a villain with a hand on the brake. That’s you, even if you were right.

**Thorough review** is what it looks like when the room can see: failure, severity, unblock, pairing, Dave-precedent. **Malicious veto** is what it looks like when they only see the -1. Same facts, different screenshot. They’re not disproving your benches. They’re filling in intent because the trail wasn’t in the thread.

So: Jordan’s gap can be the real engineering miss **and** the nickname can still stick. Those aren’t opposites. One is about the code. The other is about who got to be the obstacle in public.

You don’t need them to recant “malice” in the next two hours. You need the artifact in the room so “veto” has to compete with “here’s what broke.” The label fades when the miss is visible. It doesn’t fade because you win the argument that you were the only adult.

Okay, but like… *what if* I just open the all-hands by showing the full review thread? Let them see the unblock offer, the pairing offer, the Dave precedent, the edge-case benches. Let them see Jordan's missing data. Then ask: "Which part of this is malicious?"

Don’t open all-hands like that.

Showing the thread can help **in the right room**. Leading with *“which part of this is malicious?”* turns a company meeting into a cross-examination. People who already think you’re a gatekeeper will hear: *I’m going to make Jordan look sloppy in front of everyone, then dare you to say I’m the problem.* Even if the screenshots are clean, that *move* is what they’ll remember.

All-hands is also the wrong stage. Mixed audience, no time for RFC guts, promo-adjacent drama. Dumping Jordan’s missing benches there doesn’t look like rigor. It looks like you brought a personnel fight to a town hall.

**Jordan’s gap can still be the engineering miss.** You’re allowed to want that named. You’re not entitled to a public verdict that the nickname was unfair.

If you have to speak at all:

- One factual beat: what failed, why it was blocking, what the unblock was.
- No “malicious,” no “who’s sloppy,” no Dave-as-gotcha unless someone asks about consistency.
- Offer to walk the *review* in `#eng-review` or a working session, not the morality vote.

The thread is your defense if someone actually challenges the call. It is not an opening act. Walk in as the person who held a bar and will help land it — not the person who needs the room to recant.

You're right about the all-hands stage thing... but I still feel like everyone's already decided I'm the villain here 😩

Real talk: if I just own the block, show the unblock path, and *don't* mention Jordan at all — does that actually fix anything? Or am I walking into a room where nothing I say matters??

That feeling sucks, and it’s not imaginary — a nickname in `#eng-review` *is* a story that’s already circulating. You’re not crazy for noticing.

Owning the block, showing the unblock, and leaving Jordan’s name out of all-hands is the right *shape*. It won’t “fix” the villain edit in two hours. All-hands isn’t a court. Most people won’t reverse a Slack narrative because you were calm for ninety seconds. A few people who were on the fence will clock that you didn’t throw anyone under the bus. That’s the actual win in that room: you don’t *add* a new clip of you prosecuting Jordan.

You’re not walking into a room where *nothing* you say matters. You’re walking into a room where **almost nothing you say there is the thing that matters.** The nickname dies (or doesn’t) in the next review cycle: you pair, the benches land, the RFC ships or gets a scoped exception, and the same bar shows up on the next packet that isn’t promo-shaped. That’s when “malicious veto” has to compete with “oh, they actually meant the edge cases.”

So don’t treat all-hands as the redemption scene. Treat it as: don’t make it worse, don’t make it about Jordan, one concrete unblock, then go do the work in the channel that actually has the fight. The room has already *started* a story. You don’t beat it with a speech. You starve it.
